tips: Mash potatoes while warm and dry them on the flame briefly if watery.
recipes.name: Aloo Paratha
steps: Mix wheat flour with a pinch of salt and knead a soft dough with water. Cover and rest 15 minutes.
Mash boiled potatoes. Mix green chilli, coriander, ajwain, amchur, salt and chilli powder into a smooth stuffing.
Divide dough into equal balls. Roll one ball lightly, place stuffing in the centre, seal edges and flatten gently.
Dust with flour and roll into a round paratha of even thickness. Avoid tearing.
Heat a tawa on medium flame. Cook the paratha on both sides, applying ghee, until golden brown spots appear.
Serve hot with curd, pickle or butter.

tips: Keep stuffing dry so the paratha does not break while rolling.
recipes.name: Paneer Paratha
steps: Mix wheat flour with a pinch of salt and knead a soft dough with water. Cover and rest 15 minutes.
Mix grated paneer with onion, chilli, coriander, garam masala and salt.
Divide dough into equal balls. Roll one ball lightly, place stuffing in the centre, seal edges and flatten gently.
Dust with flour and roll into a round paratha of even thickness. Avoid tearing.
Heat a tawa on medium flame. Cook the paratha on both sides, applying ghee, until golden brown spots appear.
Serve hot with curd, pickle or butter.

tips: Keep stuffing dry so the paratha does not break while rolling.
recipes.name: Gobhi Paratha
steps: Mix wheat flour with a pinch of salt and knead a soft dough with water. Cover and rest 15 minutes.
Squeeze excess water from grated cauliflower. Mix with ginger, chilli, spices and salt. Lightly sauté 2 minutes if very moist.
Divide dough into equal balls. Roll one ball lightly, place stuffing in the centre, seal edges and flatten gently.
Dust with flour and roll into a round paratha of even thickness. Avoid tearing.
Heat a tawa on medium flame. Cook the paratha on both sides, applying ghee, until golden brown spots appear.
Serve hot with curd, pickle or butter.

tips: Keep stuffing dry so the paratha does not break while rolling.
recipes.name: Mooli Paratha
steps: Mix wheat flour with a pinch of salt and knead a soft dough with water. Cover and rest 15 minutes.
Squeeze grated radish firmly to remove water. Mix with chilli, coriander, ajwain and salt. Use the squeezed water in dough if needed.
Divide dough into equal balls. Roll one ball lightly, place stuffing in the centre, seal edges and flatten gently.
Dust with flour and roll into a round paratha of even thickness. Avoid tearing.
Heat a tawa on medium flame. Cook the paratha on both sides, applying ghee, until golden brown spots appear.
Serve hot with curd, pickle or butter.

tips: If methi is bitter, soak chopped leaves in salted water 10 minutes, then squeeze.
recipes.name: Methi Paratha
steps: Wash methi leaves thoroughly and chop finely. If bitter, soak in salted water 10 minutes and squeeze dry.
Mix flour, chopped methi, ajwain, turmeric, chilli powder and salt. Knead a soft dough with water. Rest 15 minutes.
Divide into balls and roll into medium-thick parathas.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee until both sides are golden and crisp at the edges.
Serve with curd or white butter.

tips: Keep stuffing dry so the paratha does not break while rolling.
recipes.name: Palak Paratha
steps: Blanch spinach 2 minutes, cool, and grind with green chilli into a smooth puree.
Knead wheat flour with spinach puree, cumin powder and salt into a soft dough. Rest 10 minutes.
Roll into parathas of even thickness.
Cook on tawa with ghee until light brown spots appear on both sides.
Serve hot with pickle or raita.

tips: Authentic Purvanchal stuffing uses raw mustard oil and garlic for a sharp taste.
recipes.name: Sattu Paratha
steps: Mix wheat flour with a pinch of salt and knead a soft dough with water. Cover and rest 15 minutes.
Mix sattu with mustard oil, onion, garlic, chilli, pickle masala, ajwain and salt. Add a spoon of water only if too dry.
Divide dough into equal balls. Roll one ball lightly, place stuffing in the centre, seal edges and flatten gently.
Dust with flour and roll into a round paratha of even thickness. Avoid tearing.
Heat a tawa on medium flame. Cook the paratha on both sides, applying ghee, until golden brown spots appear.
Serve hot with curd, pickle or butter.

tips: Keep stuffing dry so the paratha does not break while rolling.
recipes.name: Dal Paratha
steps: Mix wheat flour with a pinch of salt and knead a soft dough with water. Cover and rest 15 minutes.
Mash cooked chana dal. Mix ginger, chilli, garam masala and salt. Cook on low flame 2–3 minutes to dry excess moisture.
Divide dough into equal balls. Roll one ball lightly, place stuffing in the centre, seal edges and flatten gently.
Dust with flour and roll into a round paratha of even thickness. Avoid tearing.
Heat a tawa on medium flame. Cook the paratha on both sides, applying ghee, until golden brown spots appear.
Serve hot with curd, pickle or butter.

tips: Keep stuffing dry so the paratha does not break while rolling.
recipes.name: Pyaz Paratha
steps: Mix wheat flour with a pinch of salt and knead a soft dough with water. Cover and rest 15 minutes.
Mix chopped onion with chilli, coriander, ajwain and salt just before stuffing so onions do not release water.
Divide dough into equal balls. Roll one ball lightly, place stuffing in the centre, seal edges and flatten gently.
Dust with flour and roll into a round paratha of even thickness. Avoid tearing.
Heat a tawa on medium flame. Cook the paratha on both sides, applying ghee, until golden brown spots appear.
Serve hot with curd, pickle or butter.

tips: Keep stuffing dry so the paratha does not break while rolling.
recipes.name: Mix Veg Paratha

ingredients.name: Boiled mixed vegetables (carrot, peas, beans, potato), mashed

steps: Mix wheat flour with a pinch of salt and knead a soft dough with water. Cover and rest 15 minutes.
Mash boiled vegetables, mix spices and salt into a firm stuffing.
Divide dough into equal balls. Roll one ball lightly, place stuffing in the centre, seal edges and flatten gently.
Dust with flour and roll into a round paratha of even thickness. Avoid tearing.
Heat a tawa on medium flame. Cook the paratha on both sides, applying ghee, until golden brown spots appear.
Serve hot with curd, pickle or butter.

tips: Keep stuffing dry so the paratha does not break while rolling.
recipes.name: Gajar Paratha
steps: Mix wheat flour with a pinch of salt and knead a soft dough with water. Cover and rest 15 minutes.
Squeeze grated carrot lightly. Mix with chilli, coriander, cumin and salt.
Divide dough into equal balls. Roll one ball lightly, place stuffing in the centre, seal edges and flatten gently.
Dust with flour and roll into a round paratha of even thickness. Avoid tearing.
Heat a tawa on medium flame. Cook the paratha on both sides, applying ghee, until golden brown spots appear.
Serve hot with curd, pickle or butter.

tips: Keep stuffing dry so the paratha does not break while rolling.
recipes.name: Besan Paratha
steps: Mix wheat flour with a pinch of salt and knead a soft dough with water. Cover and rest 15 minutes.
Mix besan with onion, ajwain, chilli and salt. Sprinkle a few drops of water and oil to make a crumbly stuffing.
Divide dough into equal balls. Roll one ball lightly, place stuffing in the centre, seal edges and flatten gently.
Dust with flour and roll into a round paratha of even thickness. Avoid tearing.
Heat a tawa on medium flame. Cook the paratha on both sides, applying ghee, until golden brown spots appear.
Serve hot with curd, pickle or butter.

tips: Apply ghee between layers for flaky laccha-style paratha.
recipes.name: Plain Paratha
steps: Knead a soft dough with flour, salt and water. Rest 15 minutes.
Divide into balls. Roll each into a circle, brush ghee, fold into a triangle or roll like a spiral for layers.
Roll again gently to medium thickness.
Cook on a hot tawa, applying ghee on both sides, until golden and flaky.
Serve with sabzi, dal or curd.

tips: Good for digestion; serve with curd.
recipes.name: Ajwain Paratha
steps: Crush ajwain lightly and knead into flour with salt, oil and water to a soft dough. Rest 15 minutes.
Roll into medium-thick discs.
Cook on tawa with ghee until both sides are spotted golden.
Serve hot with curd or pickle.
Store leftover dough covered for same-day use.

tips: Curd keeps theplas soft for longer journeys.
recipes.name: Thepla
steps: Mix flour, besan, methi, curd, spices, salt and oil. Knead a soft dough; add a spoon of water only if needed.
Rest 10 minutes. Divide into balls and roll thin theplas.
Cook on a tawa on medium flame with little oil until both sides are golden.
Cool completely if packing for travel; they stay soft for a day.
Serve with curd, pickle or chai.

tips: Dough should be firmer than chapati dough so puris puff well.
recipes.name: Bedmi Puri
steps: Soak urad dal 4 hours. Grind coarsely with fennel, chilli, hing and salt — keep it thick, not watery.
Mix the dal paste into wheat flour with 1 tbsp oil and knead a firm dough. Rest 20 minutes.
Make small balls, roll into thick puris.
Deep fry in hot oil on medium flame until puffed and golden.
Serve with spicy aloo sabzi or kaddu sabzi.

tips: Dry the filling well or puris will open while frying.
recipes.name: Dal Puri
steps: Boil soaked chana dal until soft but not mushy. Drain and grind with ginger, chilli, fennel and salt to a thick paste.
Cook paste on low flame 3–4 minutes to remove moisture. Cool.
Knead soft dough. Stuff each dough ball with dal filling, seal and roll carefully.
Deep fry until golden and crisp.
Serve with aloo rasedar or plain curd.

tips: Low flame frying gives the khasta texture.
recipes.name: Urad Dal Kachori
steps: Grind soaked urad dal coarsely with fennel, crushed coriander, hing, chilli powder and salt. Cook filling until dry.
Rub ghee into maida, knead a tight dough with little water. Rest 30 minutes.
Stuff, seal and flatten into thick discs.
Fry on low–medium flame for 8–10 minutes until crisp and layered.
Serve with aloo sabzi and green chutney.

tips: Winter peas make the best matar kachori.
recipes.name: Matar Kachori
steps: Coarsely crush peas with ginger, chilli and fennel. Sauté in little oil with amchur and salt until dry.
Make ghee-enriched maida dough. Rest 20 minutes.
Stuff pea filling into dough balls, seal and flatten.
Deep fry on medium-low heat until golden and crisp.
Serve with green chutney or aloo sabzi.

tips: Do not over-wet the potato filling.
recipes.name: Aloo Kachori
steps: Mix mashed potato with chilli, coriander, amchur, garam masala and salt.
Prepare firm maida dough with ghee. Rest 20 minutes.
Stuff, seal and flatten into kachoris.
Fry on medium flame until crisp and golden.
Serve with tamarind chutney or raita.

tips: Same stuffing style as sattu paratha, but fried.
recipes.name: Sattu Puri
steps: Mix sattu with mustard oil, garlic, chilli, pickle masala and salt for stuffing.
Knead wheat dough. Stuff, seal and roll into thick puris.
Deep fry until puffed and golden.
Serve with aloo chokha or plain curd.
Eat fresh for the best crunch.

tips: Potato in dough keeps puris soft longer.
recipes.name: Aloo Puri
steps: Knead flour with mashed potato, ajwain, turmeric, salt and little water into a soft dough.
Roll into small puris.
Deep fry until golden and puffed.
Serve with chana or raita.
Best eaten hot.

tips: Use thick chooda, not thin Indori poha.
recipes.name: Chooda Matar
steps: Rinse thick poha once and drain. Keep slightly moist, not soggy.
Heat mustard oil, add cumin, onion and chilli. Sauté until onion softens.
Add potato and peas with turmeric and salt. Cover and cook until soft.
Add poha, mix gently on low flame 3–4 minutes so it absorbs flavours.
Finish with coriander and a squeeze of lemon. Serve hot for breakfast.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Chana Ghugni
steps: Pressure cook soaked kala chana with salt until soft but whole (3–4 whistles).
Heat mustard oil, temper cumin, sauté onion till golden, add ginger-garlic.
Add tomato and spices; cook until oil separates.
Add boiled chana with some cooking water. Simmer 10 minutes.
Garnish with onion rings and coriander. Serve as breakfast or snack.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Matar Ghugni
steps: Heat mustard oil, add cumin, onion and green chilli. Sauté until soft.
Add tomato and spices; cook till mushy.
Add peas and potato with a little water. Cover and cook until tender.
Simmer until a thick, spoonable gravy forms.
Serve with kachori, puri or plain roti.

tips: Traditional taste needs raw mustard oil and garlic in the sattu.
recipes.name: Sattu Litti
steps: Mix sattu with mustard oil, garlic, ginger, chilli, ajwain, pickle masala, lemon and salt. Filling should be crumbly and aromatic.
Knead firm wheat dough with salt and little oil. Rest 15 minutes.
Stuff dough balls with sattu, seal into round littis.
Roast on coal, in a tandoor, or bake at 200°C for 25–30 minutes, turning until cracked and browned. Alternatively cook on gas tandoor/grill.
Crack open hot littis, dunk generously in ghee. Serve with chokha.

tips: Flame-roasting gives the authentic smoky chokha flavour.
recipes.name: Litti Chokha
steps: Prepare sattu littis as in Sattu Litti recipe and keep warm in ghee.
Roast baingan, tomato and potato directly on flame until charred and soft. Peel.
Mash each separately or together with raw onion, garlic, chilli, mustard oil and salt — this is chokha.
Arrange littis with baingan chokha, aloo chokha and tamatar chokha on a plate.
Serve immediately with extra ghee and green chilli.

tips: Do not overfill or pithas may open while steaming.
recipes.name: Dal Pitha
steps: Grind soaked chana dal with ginger, chilli, cumin and salt into a coarse stuffing. Sauté briefly in mustard oil to dry.
Knead soft dough. Roll small discs, place stuffing, fold and seal like dumplings.
Steam in a steamer or idli cooker for 15–18 minutes until cooked through.
Optionally temper with mustard oil, garlic and chilli before serving.
Serve hot with chutney or ghee.

tips: In Jaunpur homes, tempered fara is a rainy-day favourite.
recipes.name: Fara / Gojha
steps: Grind chana dal with ginger, chilli and cumin into stuffing; cook till dry.
Knead hot-water rice flour dough. Make oval pockets, stuff and seal (gojha shape).
Steam 15–20 minutes until firm.
Slice steamed faras. Temper mustard oil with garlic and red chilli; toss slices until lightly crisp.
Serve with green chutney.

tips: Healthier steamed cousin of dal pakora — popular in Purvanchal kitchens.
recipes.name: Bafauri
steps: Grind soaked chana dal coarsely with ginger, garlic, chilli and cumin — keep texture, not a fine paste.
Mix salt and coriander. Shape into small freestyle dumplings with oiled hands.
Steam 12–15 minutes until cooked and springy.
Optionally pan-sear lightly in mustard oil.
Serve with coriander chutney or tomato chutney.

tips: Do not soak poha in water or it turns mushy.
recipes.name: Vegetable Poha
steps: Rinse poha in a colander, drain and fluff. Sprinkle salt, turmeric and sugar; rest 5 minutes.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds, curry leaves and peanuts; roast peanuts lightly.
Add onion and potato; cook until potato is soft.
Add poha, mix gently on low flame 2–3 minutes.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander. Serve hot.

tips: Onion-forward is the hallmark of kanda poha.
recipes.name: Kanda Poha
steps: Rinse and drain poha; season with salt, turmeric and sugar.
Temper mustard, curry leaves, peanuts and lots of onion until soft and sweet.
Add green chilli, then poha. Mix gently.
Cover 1 minute on low flame.
Serve with lemon, coriander and optionally sev.

tips: Sev on top is essential for Indori style.
recipes.name: Indori Poha
steps: Prepare seasoned poha as usual with onion tempering.
Sprinkle jeeravan or garam masala while mixing.
Plate poha, top generously with nylon sev.
Add chopped onion, coriander, lemon and pomegranate if available.
Serve immediately so sev stays crisp.

tips: Roasting suji prevents raw taste and stickiness.
recipes.name: Vegetable Upma
steps: Dry roast suji on medium flame until aromatic; keep aside.
Temper mustard, curry leaves, chilli and onion. Add vegetables; sauté 3 minutes.
Add water and salt; bring to a boil.
Lower flame, add roasted suji gradually while stirring to avoid lumps.
Cover 2 minutes. Fluff and serve with coconut chutney or lemon.

tips: Use slightly less water than suji upma.
recipes.name: Vermicelli Upma
steps: Roast vermicelli in a spoon of oil until light golden.
Temper spices and sauté onion with vegetables.
Add water and salt; bring to boil.
Add vermicelli, cook on low until water is absorbed and strands are soft.
Serve hot with coconut chutney.

tips: Spread thin for crisp edges.
recipes.name: Besan Chilla
steps: Whisk besan with water to a lump-free batter of pouring consistency.
Add onion, tomato, chilli, ajwain, turmeric and salt.
Heat a tawa, grease lightly, pour a ladle and spread into a thin circle.
Drizzle oil, cook both sides until golden and cooked in the centre.
Serve with green chutney or tomato ketchup.

tips: Do not make batter too watery.
recipes.name: Moong Dal Cheela
steps: Grind soaked moong dal with ginger, chilli and cumin to a slightly coarse batter. Add salt.
Heat non-stick or well-seasoned tawa. Pour and spread medium-thick cheela.
Cook both sides with little oil until light brown spots appear.
Optionally sprinkle chopped onion or paneer on top while cooking.
Serve with mint chutney.

tips: Spread thin for crisp edges.
recipes.name: Paneer Chilla
steps: Make besan batter. Mix in grated paneer, onion, chilli and salt.
Spread on hot tawa and cook both sides with oil until golden.
Press gently so paneer cooks into the chilla.
Cut into wedges if large.
Serve hot with chutney.

tips: Spread thin for crisp edges.
recipes.name: Suji Chilla
steps: Mix suji, curd and water; rest 15 minutes so suji softens.
Add vegetables, chilli and salt.
Spread on greased tawa; cook both sides until crisp.
Serve immediately.
Batter thickens on standing — loosen with a spoon of water if needed.

tips: Use well-fermented batter for soft idlis.
recipes.name: Idli Sambhar
steps: Grease idli moulds, pour fermented batter and steam 10–12 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Pressure cook toor dal until soft. Mash lightly.
In a pot, sauté onion and tomato, add sambar powder, tamarind water and salt. Boil 5 minutes.
Add dal and simmer. Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil; pour over sambar.
Serve soft idlis with hot sambar and coconut chutney.

tips: Tawa must be hot, then slightly cooled before spreading batter.
recipes.name: Masala Dosa
steps: Prepare potato masala: temper mustard and curry leaves, sauté onion and chilli, add turmeric and mashed potato with salt.
Heat a flat tawa. Spread dosa batter thinly in a circle. Drizzle oil.
When the underside is golden, place potato masala in the centre.
Fold the dosa and roast a few more seconds.
Serve with coconut chutney and sambar.

tips: For crisp dosa, batter should be slightly thin.
recipes.name: Plain Dosa
steps: Stir fermented batter; adjust salt and a splash of water if thick.
Heat tawa, spread thin dosa, drizzle oil on edges.
Cook until crisp and golden; flip briefly if needed.
Fold and serve hot.
Pair with chutney and sambar.

tips: Batter must be thin for the classic lace texture.
recipes.name: Rava Dosa
steps: Mix suji, rice flour, maida, cumin, chilli, onion, salt and water into a thin watery batter. Rest 20 minutes.
Heat tawa very hot. Pour batter from height in a lace pattern — do not spread with ladle.
Drizzle oil in the holes; cook until crisp and golden.
Fold and serve immediately.
Stir batter each time before pouring.

tips: Medium flame keeps the centre cooked without burning.
recipes.name: Uttapam
steps: Pour a thick circle of batter on a medium-hot tawa — thicker than dosa.
Sprinkle onion, tomato, chilli and coriander on top; press lightly.
Drizzle oil around edges. Cook until base is golden.
Flip carefully and cook the topped side 1–2 minutes.
Serve with sambar and chutney.

tips: Appe mould must be well heated before pouring.
recipes.name: Appe
steps: Mix vegetables and tempering into idli batter.
Heat appe mould, add few drops oil in each cavity.
Pour batter three-quarters full. Cover and cook 2–3 minutes.
Flip each appe with a skewer; cook until golden on both sides.
Serve with coconut chutney.

tips: Add Eno only just before steaming.
recipes.name: Dhokla
steps: Whisk besan, curd, water, turmeric, chilli-ginger, sugar, lemon and salt into a smooth batter.
Add Eno, mix briefly until frothy. Pour into a greased steamer tray immediately.
Steam 15–18 minutes until a knife comes out clean. Cool slightly and cut squares.
Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and slit chilli in oil; add a little water and sugar, pour over dhokla.
Garnish with coriander and serve.

tips: For softer daliya use more water.
recipes.name: Vegetable Daliya
steps: Dry roast daliya until aromatic.
In a pressure cooker, heat ghee, add cumin, onion, tomato and vegetables.
Add daliya, water and salt. Pressure cook 3 whistles.
Rest 5 minutes, open and fluff.
Serve with curd or pickle.

tips: Do not overfill or filling spills while toasting.
recipes.name: Paneer Sandwich
steps: Mix paneer, capsicum, onion, chaat masala and salt.
Butter bread slices, spread filling, close sandwich.
Toast on a sandwich maker or tawa until golden.
Cut diagonally and serve hot.
Optional: add green chutney inside.

tips: Boil potatoes in advance for quick assembly.
recipes.name: Vegetable Sandwich
steps: Butter bread and spread green chutney on both slices.
Layer potato, onion, tomato; sprinkle chaat masala and salt.
Close sandwich; toast lightly or serve fresh Bombay style.
Cut into triangles.
Serve with ketchup.

tips: White/shahi gravy uses more cashew and less red chilli for a milder look.
recipes.name: Shahi Paneer
steps: Soak cashews 15 minutes; grind with tomato into a smooth paste (or boil onion-tomato and blend).
Heat butter/ghee, add whole spices (bay, cardamom). Sauté paste until oil separates.
Add chilli powder, salt and a little water; simmer into a rich gravy.
Add paneer cubes and cream. Simmer 5 minutes on low — do not boil hard.
Finish with garam masala and kasuri methi. Serve with naan or roti.

tips: Add paneer at the end so it stays soft.
recipes.name: Matar Paneer
steps: Make onion-tomato masala with ginger-garlic until oil separates.
Add spices and peas; sauté 2 minutes. Add water and cook peas until soft.
Add paneer cubes and simmer 5–7 minutes.
Finish with garam masala and coriander.
Serve with roti, paratha or jeera rice.

tips: Blanching keeps the palak bright green.
recipes.name: Palak Paneer
steps: Blanch spinach 2 minutes in boiling water, cool in ice water, grind to a smooth puree.
Sauté onion, ginger-garlic and tomato; add spices.
Add spinach puree and simmer 5 minutes. Adjust salt.
Add paneer cubes; cook 4–5 minutes on low.
Optional: swirl cream. Serve with roti or jeera rice.

tips: A pinch of sugar balances tomato tang.
recipes.name: Paneer Butter Masala
steps: Blend boiled tomatoes with cashews into a smooth puree; strain if desired.
Heat butter, add cumin, then puree. Cook until thick and glossy with spices.
Add salt, sugar pinch, chilli powder and kasuri methi.
Add paneer and cream; simmer gently 5 minutes.
Finish with a dollop of butter. Serve with naan or jeera rice.

tips: High flame toss keeps capsicum crisp.
recipes.name: Kadai Paneer
steps: Dry roast coriander seeds and red chillies; crush coarsely for kadai masala.
Sauté onion petals and capsicum on high flame; keep slightly crunchy. Remove.
In same pan make onion-tomato gravy; add kadai masala and spices.
Add paneer, capsicum and onion; toss on high flame 3–4 minutes.
Finish with garam masala and ginger juliennes.

tips: Overcooking makes bhurji rubbery.
recipes.name: Paneer Bhurji
steps: Crumble paneer with hands.
Heat oil, add cumin, onion and green chilli; sauté until translucent.
Add tomato and spices; cook until soft.
Add crumbled paneer, mix on medium flame 3–4 minutes. Do not overcook.
Garnish with coriander. Serve with pav, roti or as sandwich filling.

tips: Add paneer at the end so it stays soft.
recipes.name: Paneer Do Pyaza
steps: Separate onion into petals; sauté on high flame and keep aside.
Make a tomato-onion gravy with spices.
Add paneer and the sautéed onion petals.
Simmer 5 minutes so onions stay chunky (do pyaza style).
Finish with garam masala and coriander.

tips: Add paneer at the end so it stays soft.
recipes.name: Paneer Lababdar
steps: Prepare a rich onion-tomato-cashew gravy; blend smooth.
Cook gravy with butter until oil separates; add spices and kasuri methi.
Add paneer cubes and a little cream; simmer gently.
Optionally add grated paneer into gravy for texture.
Serve with butter naan or laccha paratha.

tips: Mustard oil gives authentic achari aroma.
recipes.name: Achari Paneer
steps: Heat mustard oil to smoking point, cool slightly. Add achari spices.
Sauté onion and tomato; add pickle masala and regular spices.
Add paneer and a splash of water; coat well and simmer 5 minutes.
Finish with coriander and lemon.
Serve with missi roti or plain roti.

tips: Sauté methi well to reduce bitterness.
recipes.name: Methi Paneer
steps: Wash methi, chop, and sauté 3–4 minutes until wilted and aroma mellows.
Make onion-tomato gravy separately.
Combine methi and gravy; simmer 3 minutes.
Add paneer cubes; cook 5 minutes on low.
Serve with roti or paratha.

tips: Add koftas only at serving time.
recipes.name: Paneer Kofta
steps: Mash paneer and potato with salt, chilli and cornflour. Shape into smooth koftas.
Deep fry or shallow fry until golden. Keep aside.
Prepare smooth onion-tomato-cashew gravy; cook with spices until rich.
Add cream. Just before serving, place koftas in gravy (do not boil long or they break).
Garnish with cream and coriander. Serve with naan.

tips: Add paneer at the end so it stays soft.
recipes.name: Paneer Capsicum
steps: Sauté capsicum on high flame; keep crisp. Keep aside.
Make a semi-dry onion-tomato masala with spices.
Add paneer and capsicum; toss 4–5 minutes.
Finish with amchur and garam masala.
Serve as a dry sabzi with roti.

tips: Jalfrezi is quick-cooked — keep vegetables crisp.
recipes.name: Paneer Jalfrezi
steps: Stir-fry onion, capsicum and carrot on high flame; keep crunchy.
Add tomato and spices for a semi-dry sauce.
Add paneer strips; toss quickly.
Finish with vinegar or lemon and garam masala.
Serve hot with roti or as a side.

tips: Add paneer at the end so it stays soft.
recipes.name: Paneer Handi
steps: Prepare a yogurt and onion-tomato based gravy with aromatic spices.
Cook in a heavy-bottomed handi or pot on low flame.
Add paneer and simmer covered 8–10 minutes so flavours infuse.
Finish with cream and kasuri methi.
Serve with naan or rice.

tips: Similar to butter masala; makhani leans more tomato-butter forward.
recipes.name: Paneer Makhani
steps: Make a smooth tomato-cashew makhani base cooked in butter.
Add Kashmiri chilli for colour, salt and a pinch of sugar.
Add paneer and simmer gently with cream and kasuri methi.
Do not over-boil after adding cream.
Serve with butter naan or jeera rice.

tips: Handle stuffed paneer gently so filling does not fall out.
recipes.name: Paneer Pasanda

ingredients.name: Khoya or chopped nuts for stuffing

steps: Slice paneer into thick rectangles; slit to make a pocket. Stuff with sweetened khoya/nuts mix; secure with toothpick if needed.
Lightly pan-fry stuffed paneer; keep aside.
Prepare rich onion-tomato-cashew gravy.
Place pasanda pieces in gravy; simmer gently 5 minutes.
Finish with cream and serve with sheermal or naan.

tips: Char the tikka slightly for restaurant-style flavour.
recipes.name: Paneer Tikka Masala
steps: Marinate paneer cubes in hung curd, chilli, garam masala, salt and oil for 30 minutes. Grill or pan-sear with capsicum and onion.
Prepare a tomato-butter masala gravy separately.
Add grilled paneer tikka pieces into the gravy.
Simmer 3–4 minutes so smoky flavour mixes in.
Serve with naan or pulao.

tips: Mild, creamy and slightly sweet — avoid heavy red chilli.
recipes.name: Methi Matar Malai
steps: Sauté chopped methi until raw smell goes. Boil peas until soft.
Make a white gravy: sauté onion, cashew, ginger; grind smooth. Cook with little milk.
Add methi, peas, salt and mild spices (go easy on turmeric).
Add cream and simmer 5 minutes on low.
Serve with naan or paratha.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Aloo Gobhi
steps: Heat oil, temper cumin. Add potato and gobhi; sauté on medium-high 4 minutes.
Add turmeric, chilli, coriander powder and salt. Mix well.
Cover and cook on low, stirring occasionally, until both are tender (12–15 min).
Finish with garam masala and amchur. Optional: tomato for slight gravy.
Garnish with coriander. Serve with roti.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Aloo Matar
steps: Sauté onion in oil with cumin until golden. Add tomato and spices; cook until soft.
Add potato; sauté 3 minutes. Add peas and water.
Cover and cook until potato is soft and gravy thickens.
Add garam masala.
Serve with roti or rice.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Aloo Baingan
steps: Heat mustard oil, add cumin and onion.
Add potato first; cook 5 minutes. Add baingan, tomato and spices.
Cover and cook on low until both are soft, stirring gently so baingan does not mash too early.
Finish with coriander.
Serve with roti or dal-chawal.

tips: Sauté methi to cut bitterness.
recipes.name: Aloo Methi
steps: Sauté methi in little oil until wilted; keep aside.
In same pan temper cumin, add potato and spices; cover-cook until almost done.
Add methi, mix and cook 5 more minutes.
Finish dry or semi-dry as preferred.
Serve with dal and roti.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Aloo Beans
steps: Temper cumin in oil. Add potato and beans with spices.
Add splash of water, cover and cook until tender but beans retain bite.
Finish with amchur.
Garnish with coriander.
Serve with roti.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Aloo Capsicum
steps: Cook potato with spices until almost done.
Add capsicum; cook on medium-high so it stays slightly crunchy.
Add amchur and garam masala.
Toss well 2 minutes.
Serve as dry sabzi with roti.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Aloo Tamatar Rasedar
steps: Heat mustard oil, add cumin and hing. Add tomato and cook to a mash.
Add spices and potato cubes; mix.
Add 1.5 cups water; simmer until potato is soft and gravy is pourable.
This is classic UP-style rasedar aloo for puri.
Finish with coriander and garam masala.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Dum Aloo
steps: Boil potatoes, peel, prick with fork and shallow fry until golden.
Make onion-tomato-cashew gravy; add beaten curd carefully on low flame.
Add fried potatoes and spices; add little water.
Cover and dum-cook on low 15 minutes.
Serve with naan or rice.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Jeera Aloo
steps: Heat oil/ghee, add generous cumin until it crackles and browns lightly.
Add boiled potato, turmeric, chilli, salt and amchur.
Toss on medium-high until edges crisp slightly.
Finish with coriander.
Excellent with kadhi or dal.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Aloo Palak
steps: Sauté potato with spices until half cooked.
Add chopped spinach; cook until wilted and potato is done.
Can be dry or with little water.
Finish with garlic tadka optional.
Serve with roti or rice.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Aloo Gajar
steps: Temper cumin; add potato and carrot with spices.
Cover-cook until soft. Slight natural sweetness from carrot.
Add peas optionally in winter.
Finish with amchur.
Serve with roti.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Aloo Parwal
steps: Sauté parwal and potato in mustard oil with spices.
Cover and cook until parwal is tender but not mushy.
Finish with amchur.
Common UP summer sabzi.
Serve with dal-roti.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Aloo Lauki
steps: Temper cumin and hing. Add potato, then lauki and tomato with spices.
Add little water; cover-cook until soft.
Light home-style sabzi.
Finish with coriander.
Serve with roti.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Aloo Tinda
steps: Peel and cube tinda. Cook with potato, spices and tomato.
Cover until tender. Do not overcook or tinda becomes mushy.
Finish with amchur.
Serve with roti.
Popular North Indian summer dish.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Aloo Kaddu
steps: Temper fenugreek seeds and cumin in oil.
Add potato and kaddu with turmeric, chilli, coriander, salt.
Cook covered; mash lightly for a soft texture.
Add amchur or lemon for tang.
Serve with roti or puri.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Aloo Pyaz
steps: Fry onion petals until edges brown; keep aside.
Cook potato with spices until done.
Mix onions back; toss on high flame.
Finish with amchur.
Serve dry with dal.

tips: Raw mustard oil is essential for authentic chokha taste.
recipes.name: Aloo Chokha
steps: Boil or flame-roast potatoes until soft. Peel and mash roughly while warm.
Add raw onion, garlic, green chilli, salt and mustard oil.
Mix vigorously so oil emulsifies into the mash.
Garnish with coriander.
Serve with litti, dal-chawal or roti.

tips: Mustard oil and big potato chunks define home-style tahri.
recipes.name: Aloo Tahri
steps: Wash and soak rice 20 minutes.
Heat mustard oil, add bay leaf and cumin. Fry potato cubes until lightly golden.
Add onion, turmeric, chilli, coriander powder and salt.
Add drained rice; sauté 1 minute. Add 3 cups water. Cook covered until rice and potato are done (or 1 whistle).
Rest 5 minutes. Fluff and serve with pickle or curd — classic Purvanchal one-pot meal.

tips: Fresh winter peas are non-negotiable for real nimona flavour.
recipes.name: Matar Nimona
steps: Coarsely grind fresh peas (keep texture — not a fine paste).
Heat mustard oil to smoking point, cool slightly. Add cumin, ginger-garlic; sauté.
Add tomato and spices; cook until oil separates.
Add potato cubes and ground peas. Sauté 4–5 minutes. Add water for a thick gravy.
Simmer until potatoes are soft and nimona thickens. Finish with garam masala. Serve with plain rice — Jaunpur winter classic.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Aloo Matar Nimona
steps: Grind peas coarsely. Follow nimona method but keep potato as a prominent chunky element.
Fry potato cubes first until lightly coloured before adding pea paste.
Add tomato masala, spices and water.
Simmer until thick and aromatic.
Serve with steamed rice.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Matar Nimona with Badi
steps: Fry dried urad badis until reddish; soak in warm water 5 minutes; squeeze.
Prepare nimona base with ground peas and tomato masala.
Add badis and potato; simmer gently so badis absorb gravy without breaking.
Adjust salt and chilli.
Serve with rice — a hearty Purvanchal variation.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Matar Mushroom
steps: Clean mushrooms; sauté on high flame until moisture evaporates.
Make onion-tomato gravy; add spices.
Add peas and mushrooms; simmer 8–10 minutes.
Finish with garam masala and cream optional.
Serve with roti or jeera rice.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Matar Masala
steps: Make a thick onion-tomato masala.
Add peas and little water; cook until soft and gravy coats the peas.
Add garam masala.
Garnish with coriander.
Serve with paratha or puri.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Matar Pulao
steps: Soak rice 20 minutes. Heat ghee, fry whole spices and onion until golden.
Add peas; sauté 1 minute. Add drained rice; coat in ghee.
Add 2.75 cups water and salt. Cook covered on low until done (or pressure 1 whistle).
Rest 5 minutes; fluff.
Serve with raita or curry.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Matar Tahri
steps: Like aloo tahri, but add fresh peas with the potato.
Fry potato in mustard oil, add spices, peas and rice.
Add water and cook until fluffy.
Rest and serve with mango pickle.
Winter favourite across Awadh and Purvanchal.

tips: Add koftas late so they do not break.
recipes.name: Matar Kofta
steps: Mix mashed peas, potato, besan, salt and chilli; shape koftas and fry until golden.
Prepare onion-tomato gravy.
Add koftas just before serving; simmer 3 minutes.
Garnish with coriander.
Serve with roti or pulao.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Matar Aloo Rasedar
steps: Make tomato-based thin gravy with cumin tadka.
Add potato and peas; add enough water for a rasedar (soupy) consistency.
Simmer until soft.
Finish with garam masala.
Serve with plain rice or puri.

tips: Dry bhindi well to avoid sliminess.
recipes.name: Bhindi Masala
steps: Wash and thoroughly dry bhindi; cut into pieces.
Sauté in oil on medium flame until sticky threads reduce and edges colour.
Add onion, tomato and spices; cook until masala coats bhindi.
Finish with amchur.
Serve with roti and dal.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Bhindi Do Pyaza
steps: Cook bhindi until no longer sticky.
Add lots of onion petals; cook until soft but chunky.
Add spices and amchur.
Keep semi-dry.
Serve with dal-roti.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Kurkuri Bhindi
steps: Toss bhindi strips with besan, rice flour, chilli, amchur and salt.
Deep or shallow fry until crisp.
Drain on paper.
Serve as side or snack.
Sprinkle chaat masala.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Aloo Bhindi
steps: Cook potato and bhindi separately until nearly done, then combine with spices.
Or cook potato first, then add bhindi so both finish together.
Keep dry.
Finish with amchur.
Serve with roti.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Bharwa Bhindi
steps: Slit bhindi lengthwise. Mix dry spice stuffing with salt and oil.
Stuff each bhindi.
Shallow fry covered on low flame, turning occasionally, until cooked.
Do not add water.
Serve with dal.

tips: Add curd on low flame only.
recipes.name: Dahi Bhindi
steps: Fry bhindi until cooked and non-sticky; keep aside.
Make a light onion masala; lower flame and add whisked curd mixed with spices.
Stir continuously so curd does not split.
Add bhindi; simmer 3 minutes.
Serve with roti or rice.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Gobhi Matar
steps: Sauté gobhi florets until lightly golden.
Add peas, tomato and spices; cover-cook until tender.
Finish with garam masala.
Serve with roti.
Winter staple.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Gobhi Masala
steps: Fry gobhi lightly. Make onion-tomato gravy.
Combine and simmer until florets are soft but hold shape.
Finish with kasuri methi.
Serve with naan or roti.
Can be made gravy-style.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Gobhi Do Pyaza
steps: Cook gobhi with spices until almost done.
Add generous onion petals; cook until soft and fragrant.
Keep semi-dry.
Finish with amchur.
Serve with roti.

tips: Open-flame roasting gives smoky flavour.
recipes.name: Baingan Bharta
steps: Flame-roast baingan until skin chars and flesh collapses. Peel and mash.
Sauté onion, garlic, tomato and spices until oil separates.
Add mashed baingan; cook 8–10 minutes on medium.
Finish with coriander and mustard oil optional.
Serve with roti or bajra roti.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Baingan Chokha
steps: Roast baingan and tomato on flame. Peel and mash with raw onion, garlic, chilli.
Add salt and raw mustard oil; mix vigorously.
No frying — this is chokha, not bharta.
Serve with litti or dal-chawal.
Purvanchal essential.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Bharwa Baingan
steps: Slit baingan in a cross. Stuff with dry spice mix and salt.
Shallow cook in oil on low, covered, turning gently.
Cook until soft throughout.
Serve with dal and roti.
Use mustard oil for UP taste.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Baingan Masala
steps: Shallow fry baingan pieces; drain.
Make onion-tomato gravy; add baingan and simmer.
Finish with garam masala.
Serve with roti or rice.
Adjust gravy thickness as preferred.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Lauki Chana Dal
steps: Pressure cook chana dal until almost soft (not mushy).
In a pan make cumin-onion-tomato tadka; add lauki and spices.
Add dal and water; simmer until lauki is tender and flavours marry.
Finish with ghee tadka of garlic optional.
Serve with roti or rice.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Lauki Kofta
steps: Mix squeezed lauki with besan, salt and chilli; shape koftas and fry.
Prepare gravy; add koftas at the end.
Simmer gently 3–4 minutes.
Serve with roti or pulao.
Squeeze lauki well or koftas break.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Lauki Tamatar
steps: Temper cumin; add tomato and cook soft.
Add lauki and spices with little water.
Cook until soft and lightly mashy.
Comfort home sabzi.
Serve with roti.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Lauki Aloo
steps: Cook potato and lauki together with cumin tadka and spices.
Cover until soft.
Light everyday sabzi.
Finish with coriander.
Serve with dal-roti.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Tinda Masala
steps: Sauté onion-tomato; add tinda and spices.
Cover-cook until soft but not mushy.
Finish with amchur.
Serve with roti.
Summer vegetable.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Bharwa Tinda
steps: Hollow or slit tinda; stuff with spice mix.
Cook covered on low in oil until tender.
Turn occasionally.
Serve with dal.
Patience on low flame is key.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Parwal Aloo
steps: Cook parwal and potato with spices in mustard oil.
Cover until tender.
Finish with amchur.
UP summer favourite.
Serve with roti.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Bharwa Parwal
steps: Scrape parwal lightly, slit and stuff.
Shallow fry on low until cooked through.
Serve with dal-chawal.
Fennel in stuffing is traditional.
Do not rush the cooking.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Parwal Masala
steps: Sauté parwal with onion-tomato masala and spices.
Cook covered until soft.
Keep semi-dry.
Serve with roti.
Simple weekday sabzi.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: UP Style Kaddu Sabzi
steps: Temper methi seeds and cumin in mustard oil — do not burn methi.
Add kaddu, turmeric, chilli, coriander, salt.
Cover-cook; mash lightly for soft texture.
Add amchur or grated raw mango in season.
Classic with puri in Purvanchal.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Khatti Meethi Kaddu
steps: Cook kaddu with spices until soft.
Add jaggery and amchur; mash lightly.
Balance sweet-sour to taste.
Serve with puri or roti.
Festive and everyday both.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Bharwa Karela
steps: Scrape karela, slit, rub salt; rest 20 minutes; squeeze bitterness.
Stuff with spiced onion mix.
Shallow fry on low until cooked and browned.
Serve with dal-roti.
Salt-rubbing is important.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Karela Pyaz
steps: Salt-rub and squeeze karela slices.
Fry until almost cooked; add onion and spices.
Cook until onion softens and bitterness mellows.
Finish with amchur.
Serve with bajra roti or wheat roti.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Cabbage Matar
steps: Temper cumin; add cabbage and peas with spices.
Cover briefly then cook open so cabbage does not go watery.
Finish with garam masala.
Serve with roti.
Quick sabzi.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Gajar Matar
steps: Cook carrot and peas with cumin tadka and spices.
Slightly sweet, lightly spiced.
Cover until tender.
Serve with roti or as side.
Winter classic.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Mooli Aloo
steps: Temper ajwain or cumin; add potato and mooli with spices.
Cover-cook; add chopped leaves if available.
Finish with amchur.
Serve with dal.
Winter sabzi.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Palak Corn
steps: Blanch and puree spinach or chop and cook.
Sauté with mild spices; add boiled corn.
Optional cream for restaurant style.
Serve with roti or rice.
Mild and kid-friendly.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Palak Aloo
steps: Cook potato with spices; add chopped spinach.
Cook until spinach wilts and water dries.
Garlic tadka optional.
Serve with roti or rice.
Everyday green sabzi.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Palak Chana
steps: Make spinach base with onion-tomato or simple cumin tadka.
Add boiled chana; simmer 10 minutes.
Finish with garam masala.
Serve with rice or roti.
Protein-rich.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Methi Aloo
steps: Same approach as aloo methi — sauté methi, cook potato, combine.
Keep dry.
Winter staple.
Serve with dal.
Balance methi bitterness with a pinch of sugar if needed.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Mushroom Masala
steps: Sauté mushrooms until water dries.
Add to onion-tomato gravy; simmer 8 minutes.
Finish with cream optional.
Serve with roti or rice.
Do not overcrowd pan when sautéing.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Soya Matar
steps: Soak soya in hot water; squeeze well.
Cook in onion-tomato masala with peas and spices.
Simmer until gravy thickens.
Serve with roti or rice.
Budget protein curry.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Stuffed Capsicum
steps: Hollow capsicum; stuff with spiced mashed potato (or paneer mix).
Bake or shallow cook covered until capsicum softens.
Turn gently.
Serve as main with roti or raita.
Do not overfill.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Tawa Mix Veg

ingredients.name: Pav bhaji masala or garam masala

steps: Chop veggies uniformly. Cook on a wide tawa with butter/oil and spices.
Mash lightly for tawa texture.
Keep semi-dry and robustly spiced.
Finish with lemon and coriander.
Serve with roti or pav.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Vegetable Korma
steps: Parboil vegetables. Make a mild onion-cashew or curd gravy with whole spices.
Add vegetables; simmer gently.
Keep gravy rich but not fiery.
Finish with cream or garam masala.
Serve with pulao or naan.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Gatte Ki Sabzi
steps: Knead besan with oil, ajwain, chilli, salt and little water into a firm dough. Roll into cylinders.
Boil in water 10–12 minutes until cooked; cool, cut into discs (gatte).
Make a spiced curd gravy: whisk curd with spices, cook on low with tadka until it thickens without splitting.
Add gatte; simmer 8–10 minutes.
Serve with bajra roti or rice — Rajasthani classic.

tips: Consistency should be pourable, not too thick.
recipes.name: Dal Tadka
steps: Wash and pressure cook toor dal with turmeric and salt until soft (3–4 whistles). Mash lightly.
In a pan heat ghee, add cumin, hing, garlic, dried red chilli and onion; sauté until golden.
Add tomato and chilli powder; cook briefly.
Pour tadka over dal. Simmer 5 minutes. Adjust consistency with hot water.
Finish with coriander and a spoon of ghee. Serve with rice or roti.

tips: Dal fry = dal cooked into the fried masala.
recipes.name: Dal Fry
steps: Cook toor dal until soft.
Prepare a thicker onion-tomato base fried well in ghee/oil with ginger-garlic.
Add dal into the masala (unlike tadka poured on top) and simmer 8–10 minutes.
The dal should be slightly thicker than home tadka dal.
Garnish with coriander and serve with jeera rice.

tips: Overnight soak and long simmer make restaurant-style creaminess.
recipes.name: Dal Makhani
steps: Soak whole urad and few rajma overnight. Pressure cook until very soft (6–8 whistles); mash some against the pot.
Prepare tomato puree cooked in butter with ginger-garlic and spices.
Add cooked dal; simmer on low at least 20–30 minutes, stirring often.
Add butter and cream; simmer 5 more minutes.
Serve with naan or rice. Slow cooking is the secret.

tips: Consistency should be pourable, not too thick.
recipes.name: Moong Dal
steps: Wash moong dal; cook with turmeric until soft (it cooks faster than toor).
Temper ghee with cumin, hing, green chilli and garlic.
Add to dal with salt; simmer 5 minutes.
Optional: add chopped spinach for dal palak style later.
Serve with rice — light and easy to digest.

tips: Consistency should be pourable, not too thick.
recipes.name: Masoor Dal
steps: Cook masoor dal with turmeric until soft and creamy.
Temper mustard oil or ghee with cumin, garlic and onion.
Add tomato and spices; mix into dal.
Simmer briefly.
Serve with rice or roti.

tips: Consistency should be pourable, not too thick.
recipes.name: Chana Dal
steps: Soak chana dal 30 minutes. Pressure cook until soft but grainy.
Temper ghee with cumin, hing and whole red chilli.
Add onion, ginger and tomato; cook into masala.
Mix dal; add garam masala. Simmer 8 minutes.
Serve thick with roti — classic North Indian.

tips: Watch the cooker — urad froths and can block the vent.
recipes.name: Urad Dal
steps: Wash split urad; cook carefully (it froths) with turmeric until soft.
Temper generously with ghee, cumin, hing and garlic.
Add to dal with salt and chilli.
Simmer; consistency should be creamy.
Serve with rice or bajra roti.

tips: Consistency should be pourable, not too thick.
recipes.name: Mix Dal
steps: Mix equal parts of 3–4 dals; soak 20 minutes; pressure cook with turmeric.
Prepare onion-tomato tadka in ghee.
Combine and simmer 10 minutes for flavours to blend.
Adjust thickness.
Serve with jeera rice or roti.

tips: Consistency should be pourable, not too thick.
recipes.name: Panchmel Dal
steps: Combine five dals; soak; pressure cook until soft.
Make a Rajasthani-style tadka with ghee, cumin, cloves and red chilli.
Add to dal with coriander powder and garam masala; simmer.
Should be thick enough to eat with baati.
Serve with dal baati churma or plain rice.

tips: Consistency should be pourable, not too thick.
recipes.name: Dal Palak
steps: Cook dal until soft.
Add chopped spinach and simmer 5–7 minutes.
Temper garlic and cumin in ghee; pour over.
Adjust salt and chilli.
Nutritious everyday dal.

tips: Golden garlic, not bitter black garlic.
recipes.name: Lahsun Dal
steps: Cook toor dal soft and mashy.
Heat ghee; fry lots of sliced garlic until golden (not burnt).
Add dried red chilli and cumin; pour over dal.
Simmer 3 minutes so garlic flavour infuses.
Serve hot with steamed rice — monsoon comfort food.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Punjabi Chole

ingredients.name: Tea bag or tea leaves for colour

steps: Pressure cook chickpeas with salt and tea until soft; reserve stock.
Prepare onion-tomato masala; add chole masala and amchur.
Add chole with stock; mash a few for thickness. Simmer 15 minutes.
Finish with ginger juliennes and coriander.
Serve with bhature, puri or rice.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Pindi Chole
steps: Cook chole with tea and spices until dark and soft.
Dry out most liquid; toss with oil, crushed spices and anardana for a dryish finish.
No heavy onion-tomato gravy — spice-forward dry style.
Rest 10 minutes before serving.
Classic with kulcha.

tips: Make chole slightly thinner for rice.
recipes.name: Chole Chawal
steps: Prepare Punjabi chole as in that recipe.
Cook plain steamed rice.
Serve chole over or beside rice with onion and lemon.
Optional: add a spoon of ghee on rice.
Complete comforting meal plate.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Kala Chana Masala
steps: Pressure cook kala chana until soft.
Make onion-tomato masala; add chana and simmer 12 minutes.
Mash a few for body.
Finish with garam masala.
Serve with rice or roti — also used as navratri/prasad style dry sometimes.

tips: Closely related to chana-ghugni; slightly masala-heavier snack version.
recipes.name: Kala Chana Ghugni
steps: Same family as chana ghugni — spicy, mustard-oil forward, breakfast/snack style.
Cook chana soft; prepare onion-tomato mustard oil masala.
Simmer together; keep slightly thick.
Top with chopped onion and lemon.
Serve in bowls with puffed rice optional.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Rajma Masala
steps: Pressure cook soaked rajma until very soft (critical).
Prepare deep brown onion-tomato gravy.
Add rajma with cooking water; simmer 15–20 minutes; mash a few beans.
Finish with garam masala and coriander.
Serve with hot rice.

tips: Rajma must be melt-soft.
recipes.name: Rajma Chawal
steps: Cook rajma masala until thick and creamy.
Plate steamed rice with a ladle of rajma.
Add a touch of ghee on rice.
Serve with onion salad.
Sunday favourite across North India.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Kashmiri Rajma
steps: Use small red Kashmiri beans if available; cook until soft.
Gravy is lighter on garam masala, with fennel and dry ginger notes.
Simmer long for a silky broth.
Serve with rice.
Distinct from Punjabi restaurant rajma.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Lobia Curry
steps: Pressure cook lobia until soft.
Make onion-tomato curry base; add lobia and simmer.
Adjust to medium gravy.
Finish with garam masala.
Serve with roti or rice.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Lobia Masala
steps: Cook lobia soft. Prepare a thicker masala than curry style.
Add lobia; cook until gravy clings to beans.
Optional capsicum for crunch.
Serve with roti.
Semi-dry finish.

tips: Whisk besan into curd smoothly before heating to avoid lumps.
recipes.name: Punjabi Kadhi Pakora
steps: Whisk curd and besan with water, turmeric and salt. Cook on medium, stirring, until it boils and thickens 15–20 minutes.
Make onion pakoras from besan batter; deep fry until golden.
Prepare tadka with ghee, cumin, hing, chilli; pour into kadhi.
Add pakoras; simmer 5 minutes so they soak slightly.
Serve with steamed rice.

tips: Sour curd is important for Rajasthani kadhi.
recipes.name: Rajasthani Kadhi
steps: Make a thinner sour kadhi with besan-curd; cook well.
Temper with ghee, cumin, cloves, mustard and red chilli — more aromatic and sharp.
Usually without large pakoras, or with small gatte/boondi.
Should taste distinctly sour and spicy.
Serve with bajra roti or rice.

tips: Whisk besan into curd smoothly before heating to avoid lumps.
recipes.name: UP Style Kadhi
steps: Whisk besan-curd thinner than Punjabi kadhi; cook until it no longer tastes raw.
Pakoras are optional; many homes serve plain kadhi.
Tadka with mustard oil or ghee, cumin, hing and dried red chilli.
Slightly lighter body than Punjabi version.
Serve with rice and aloo chokha optional.

tips: Slightly thinner kadhi pours better over rice.
recipes.name: Kadhi Chawal
steps: Prepare Punjabi or UP kadhi.
Cook plain rice.
Serve kadhi generously over rice.
Add ghee on top if desired.
Comfort meal for rainy days.

tips: Whisk besan into curd smoothly before heating to avoid lumps.
recipes.name: Boondi Kadhi
steps: Prepare kadhi base and cook thoroughly.
Add tadka.
Soak boondi briefly in warm water, squeeze, and add to kadhi 5 minutes before serving.
Do not over-soak or boondi turns mushy.
Serve with rice.

tips: Do not stir vigorously after adding water.
recipes.name: Vegetable Pulao
steps: Soak rice 20 minutes. Heat ghee; fry bay, cumin, clove; sauté onion.
Add vegetables; sauté 2 minutes. Add rice; coat in ghee.
Add 2.75 cups water and salt. Cook covered on low until done.
Rest 5 minutes; fluff with fork.
Serve with raita or curry.

tips: Brown cumin lightly without burning.
recipes.name: Jeera Rice
steps: Soak rice 15 minutes. Heat ghee; crackle cumin until aromatic and lightly browned.
Add drained rice; sauté 1 minute.
Add water and salt; cook until fluffy.
Rest and fluff.
Perfect with dal makhani or shahi paneer.

tips: Add paneer late so it stays soft.
recipes.name: Paneer Pulao
steps: Lightly pan-fry paneer cubes; keep aside.
Make pulao base with spices, peas and rice.
Cook rice; gently fold in paneer at the end.
Rest 5 minutes.
Serve with raita.

tips: Balance salt and slight sweetness carefully.
recipes.name: Kashmiri Pulao
steps: Soak saffron in warm milk.
Fry dry fruits in ghee; keep aside. Cook rice with whole spices, salt and a touch of sugar.
When almost done, add saffron milk and fried dry fruits.
Dum for 5 minutes.
Serve mildly sweet aromatic pulao with spicy curry.

tips: Rice must be only 70% cooked before dum.
recipes.name: Vegetable Biryani
steps: Parboil rice with whole spices until 70% cooked; drain.
Cook vegetables in curd-spice masala until semi-done and aromatic.
Layer vegetable masala and rice in a heavy pot; sprinkle fried onion, mint, saffron milk and ghee.
Seal and dum-cook on low 20 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes; gently mix and serve with raita.

tips: Do not overcook paneer in marinade pan.
recipes.name: Paneer Biryani
steps: Marinate paneer in curd and spices 20 minutes; shallow fry lightly.
Parboil rice. Layer paneer masala and rice with fried onion and mint.
Dum-cook 20 minutes on low.
Rest and serve with salan or raita.
Handle layers gently when serving.

tips: High flame and cold rice prevent sogginess.
recipes.name: Veg Fried Rice
steps: Use cold leftover rice for best texture.
Heat oil on high; stir-fry garlic and vegetables quickly.
Add rice, soy sauce, vinegar, salt and pepper; toss on high flame.
Do not mash rice.
Serve with chilli paneer or manchurian.

tips: Add lemon off the flame to keep brightness.
recipes.name: Lemon Rice
steps: Temper mustard, dals, peanuts, curry leaves and green chilli in oil.
Add turmeric; switch off flame; add lemon juice and salt.
Mix into cooled cooked rice gently.
Adjust lemon to taste.
Serve with curd or papad.

tips: Ripe tomatoes give better colour and tang.
recipes.name: Tomato Rice
steps: Temper spices; sauté onion and tomatoes with chilli powder and salt until jammy.
Add soaked rice and water; cook until done.
Or mix tomato masala into leftover rice.
Rest and fluff.
Serve with curd.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Vegetable Tahri
steps: Heat mustard oil; fry potato and gobhi lightly.
Add spices, peas and soaked rice.
Add water; cook like tahri until everything is done.
Rest and serve with pickle and papad.
One-pot Awadhi/Purvanchal meal.

tips: More water = softer hospital-style khichdi.
recipes.name: Moong Dal Khichdi
steps: Wash moong dal and rice together (1:1.5 dal:rice or equal).
Temper ghee with cumin and hing; add dal-rice, turmeric, salt and water (about 4 cups for 1 cup mix).
Pressure cook 3–4 whistles until soft and porridge-like.
Add more ghee on top.
Serve with kaddu sabzi, papad and pickle.

tips: More water = softer hospital-style khichdi.
recipes.name: Vegetable Khichdi
steps: Same as moong khichdi but add mixed vegetables with the rice-dal.
Cook until soft.
Temper with ghee and cumin.
Comforting one-pot meal.
Adjust water for softer or grainier texture.

tips: More water = softer hospital-style khichdi.
recipes.name: Masala Khichdi
steps: Sauté onion, tomato and spices before adding rice and dal.
Add vegetables optional.
Pressure cook until soft.
More robustly spiced than plain khichdi.
Serve with curd.

tips: More water = softer hospital-style khichdi.
recipes.name: Bajra Khichdi
steps: Use bajra (pearl millet) with moong dal.
Soak bajra longer; cook with extra water until soft.
Ghee-cumin tadka.
Winter Rajasthani/North Indian special.
Serve with kadhi or ghee.

tips: More water = softer hospital-style khichdi.
recipes.name: Palak Khichdi
steps: Add pureed or chopped spinach to moong-rice khichdi while cooking.
Cook until soft and green.
Garlic-ghee tadka.
Nutritious and mild.
Serve with curd or papad.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Banarasi Aloo Tamatar
steps: Temper cumin and hing in mustard oil. Add tomatoes; cook to a mash.
Add spices and potato; add water for a bright red rasedar gravy.
Simmer until potato is soft.
Slightly tangy — Banaras home style.
Serve with plain rice or roti.

tips: Use ripe red tomatoes for authentic tang.
recipes.name: Banarasi Tamatar Chaat
steps: Chop tomatoes; cook on a tawa with butter, chilli, salt and chaat masala until soft but not fully sauce.
Add boiled potato cubes; mash lightly with tomatoes.
The mixture should be tangy, spicy and slightly mushy.
Top with sev and coriander.
Serve hot as Banarasi street-style chaat.

tips: Flame roast for authentic taste.
recipes.name: Tamatar Chokha
steps: Roast tomatoes on flame until charred and soft. Peel.
Mash with onion, garlic, chilli, salt and mustard oil.
Serve with litti or rice.
No cooking in pan needed after roasting.
Smoky flavour is key.

tips: Each vegetable can also be served separately.
recipes.name: Mix Chokha
steps: Flame-roast baingan, tomato and boil/roast potato.
Peel and mash all together with onion, garlic, chilli, salt and mustard oil.
Mix vigorously.
Serve as a trio chokha plate with litti or sattu paratha.
Adjust mustard oil to taste.

tips: Mix paste first to avoid lumps.
recipes.name: Sattu Drink – Namkeen
steps: Add sattu to a glass; slowly mix with a little water to make a lump-free paste.
Add remaining cold water, salt, cumin, lemon and a drop of mustard oil.
Optional: onion and green chilli for Jaunpur-style punch.
Stir well and drink immediately.
Cooling summer staple across Purvanchal.

tips: Milk version is richer; water is lighter.
recipes.name: Sattu Drink – Sweet
steps: Make a smooth sattu paste with little liquid.
Add water or milk and dissolve jaggery/sugar.
Add cardamom if using.
Serve chilled.
Energy drink for hot afternoons.

tips: Fry puris fresh and serve immediately.
recipes.name: Bedmi Puri with Aloo Sabzi
steps: Prepare bedmi puri as in Bedmi Puri recipe.
Prepare aloo tamatar rasedar sabzi.
Serve hot puris with a bowl of spicy aloo.
Add pickle and fried green chilli on the side.
Iconic Purvanchal breakfast plate.

tips: Kaddu should be soft and lightly mashed.
recipes.name: Puri with Kaddu Sabzi
steps: Knead firm dough; roll and deep fry puris until puffed.
Prepare UP-style kaddu sabzi (sweet-tangy).
Serve puris with kaddu.
Common festive and Sunday breakfast in Jaunpur homes.
Eat hot.

tips: Baati dough must be stiff; soft dough will not bake right.
recipes.name: Dal Baati Churma
steps: Knead stiff dough with flour, ghee, ajwain and salt. Shape hard baatis with a crack on top.
Bake at 200°C / roast on charcoal or in a gas tandoor until deep brown and cooked inside (35–45 min). Dunk hot baatis in melted ghee.
Cook panchmel dal with tadka until thick.
For churma: crush 2–3 baatis, mix with ghee and powdered sugar/jaggery.
Serve baati broken into dal, with churma on the side.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Papad Ki Sabzi
steps: Roast or lightly fry papad; break into pieces.
Make a thin curd-besan gravy with spices on low flame (like kadhi).
Add papad pieces; simmer 3–4 minutes only.
Do not overcook or papad dissolves completely.
Rajasthani quick sabzi when fresh vegetables are scarce.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Ker Sangri
steps: Soak ker and sangri overnight; boil until soft; drain.
Temper oil with spices; add ker-sangri and yoghurt-spice mix.
Cook until oil separates and flavours intensify.
Should taste tangy, spicy and desert-aromatic.
Serve with bajra roti and ghee.

tips: Make one roti at a time; dough stiffens quickly.
recipes.name: Bajra Roti
steps: Knead bajra flour with warm water and salt into a soft dough (knead portions as you go — it dries fast).
Pat with hands into a thick roti (rolling is harder than wheat).
Cook on hot tawa; finish directly on flame for char if comfortable doing so.
Smear with ghee.
Serve with ker sangri, gatte, lasun chutney or jaggery.

tips: Besan makes roti protein-rich and flavourful.
recipes.name: Missi Roti
steps: Mix flours with ajwain, chilli, salt, oil and onion. Knead soft dough.
Roll medium-thick rotis.
Cook on tawa with ghee until spotted brown.
Serve with white butter, pickle or dal.
Hearty Rajasthani/Punjabi flatbread.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Jodhpuri Aloo
steps: Boil and peel potatoes; prick and shallow fry.
Make a spicy yoghurt-based Rajasthani gravy with fennel and red chilli.
Add potatoes; simmer until coated and flavourful.
Fairly dry to semi-gravy.
Serve with missi roti or bajra roti.

tips: Adjust water for dry or gravy style as preferred at home.
recipes.name: Mangodi Aloo
steps: Lightly fry mangodi; soak briefly.
Cook potato-tomato masala; add mangodi and water.
Simmer until mangodi softens and gravy thickens.
Rajasthani pantry special.
Serve with roti.

tips: Extra ghee is traditional.
recipes.name: Rajasthani Khichdi
steps: Dry roast moong dal lightly. Cook with rice, turmeric, salt and water until soft.
Prepare a generous ghee tadka with cumin, cloves and red chilli.
Pour over khichdi.
Serve with kadhi, papad and ghee.
Simpler than festivities but distinctly Rajasthani in tadka.

recipes.name: Aloo Tikki
steps: Mash potatoes with spices, chilli, coriander and binder.
Shape flat tikkis.
Shallow fry on medium until crisp and golden both sides.
Serve with chutneys or as chaat with curd and sev.
Keep mash dry for crispiness.

recipes.name: Papdi Chaat
steps: Arrange papdi on a plate; top with potato and chickpeas.
Spoon whipped salted curd, both chutneys.
Sprinkle chaat masala, cumin powder and sev.
Serve immediately before papdi softens.
Garnish with coriander.

recipes.name: Dahi Bhalla
steps: Grind urad to fluffy batter; whisk well. Fry soft vadas; soak in warm water; squeeze.
Whisk curd with salt and a little sugar.
Place bhallas in curd; top with chutneys, cumin and chilli powder.
Chill before serving.
Soft soak is the hallmark.

recipes.name: Bhel Puri
steps: Mix murmura with chutneys, onion, tomato, potato and spices just before eating.
Add sev and lemon.
Toss quickly.
Serve immediately while crisp.
Do not premix or it turns soggy.

tips: Low-medium frying gives crisp layers.
recipes.name: Samosa
steps: Make stiff maida dough with ghee; rest 20 minutes.
Prepare dry spiced potato-peas filling.
Shape cones, fill, seal into triangles.
Deep fry on medium-low until golden and crisp (not high flame).
Serve with chutney.

tips: Batter should coat well; not too thin.
recipes.name: Aloo Pakoda
steps: Make a thick besan batter with ajwain, chilli, salt and water.
Dip prepared aloo pieces in batter.
Deep fry on medium flame until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with green chutney and chai — especially in rain.

tips: Batter should coat well; not too thin.
recipes.name: Pyaz Pakoda
steps: Make a thick besan batter with ajwain, chilli, salt and water.
Dip prepared pyaz pieces in batter.
Deep fry on medium flame until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with green chutney and chai — especially in rain.

tips: Batter should coat well; not too thin.
recipes.name: Paneer Pakoda
steps: Make a thick besan batter with ajwain, chilli, salt and water.
Dip prepared paneer pieces in batter.
Deep fry on medium flame until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with green chutney and chai — especially in rain.

tips: Batter should coat well; not too thin.
recipes.name: Bread Pakoda

ingredients.name: Bread slices stuffed with spiced potato

steps: Make a thick besan batter with ajwain, chilli, salt and water.
Dip prepared bread pieces in batter.
Deep fry on medium flame until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with green chutney and chai — especially in rain.

tips: Chill shaped cutlets 10 minutes before frying.
recipes.name: Vegetable Cutlet
steps: Mash boiled vegetables with spices and some breadcrumbs.
Shape cutlets; coat in breadcrumbs.
Shallow fry until crisp both sides.
Serve with chutney or ketchup.
Mixture must be dry enough to hold shape.

tips: More butter = more street-style flavour.
recipes.name: Pav Bhaji
steps: Boil potato and vegetables; mash.
On a wide tawa, cook tomatoes in butter with pav bhaji masala and chilli.
Add mashed veg; mash together with butter and water to a soft bhaji.
Toast pav with butter on the tawa.
Serve bhaji with pav, onion and lemon.

tips: High heat keeps noodles from turning soggy.
recipes.name: Veg Hakka Noodles
steps: Boil noodles until just done; rinse in cold water; toss with oil.
Stir-fry garlic and vegetables on high flame.
Add noodles, sauces and salt; toss quickly.
Do not overcook.
Serve hot with chilli sauce.

tips: Use heavy-bottomed pan to avoid burning.
recipes.name: Suji Halwa
steps: Roast suji in ghee on medium until golden and aromatic.
Boil water with sugar and cardamom separately.
Carefully add hot syrup to roasted suji while stirring.
Cook until ghee separates and halwa leaves the sides.
Garnish with nuts. Prasad-style classic.

tips: Use heavy-bottomed pan to avoid burning.
recipes.name: Besan Halwa
steps: Roast besan in ghee patiently until deep golden and nutty (do not rush).
Add warm milk/water carefully while stirring.
Add sugar and cardamom; cook until glossy and thick.
Garnish with nuts.
Slow roasting is everything.

tips: Use heavy-bottomed pan to avoid burning.
recipes.name: Moong Dal Halwa
steps: Cook ground moong dal in ghee on low, stirring continuously until colour deepens (20–30 min).
Add milk and sugar; cook until thick and ghee oozes.
Add khoya if using.
Garnish with nuts.
Festive Rajasthani/North Indian special.

tips: Use heavy-bottomed pan to avoid burning.
recipes.name: Gajar Halwa
steps: Cook grated carrot in milk on medium, stirring, until milk reduces and carrot softens.
Add sugar; cook further until thick.
Add ghee and khoya; roast until glossy.
Finish with cardamom and nuts.
Winter favourite — use red Delhi carrots if possible.

tips: Use heavy-bottomed pan to avoid burning.
recipes.name: Kheer
steps: Wash and soak rice 20 minutes. Boil milk; add rice.
Cook on low, stirring often, until rice is soft and milk thickens (35–45 min).
Add sugar and cardamom; cook 5 more minutes.
Garnish with nuts. Serve warm or chilled.
Do not rush — slow reduction makes creamy kheer.

tips: Use heavy-bottomed pan to avoid burning.
recipes.name: Seviyan Kheer
steps: Roast vermicelli in ghee until golden.
Add milk; cook until soft and slightly thick.
Add sugar and cardamom.
Garnish with nuts.
Quick festive dessert — Eid and family dinners.

tips: Medium flame keeps insides cooked without burning.
recipes.name: Malpua
steps: Make a flowing batter of maida, milk, fennel and a spoon of sugar. Rest 20 minutes.
Prepare sugar syrup with cardamom to one-thread consistency.
Fry ladlefuls of batter in medium-hot ghee until golden and crisp at edges.
Dip malpuas in warm syrup.
Serve with rabri optional — Holi/festive special in Jaunpur homes too.

tips: Seal edges well or filling leaks while frying.
recipes.name: Gujiya
steps: Make firm maida dough with ghee; rest.
Roast khoya; cool; mix sugar, nuts and cardamom for filling.
Roll discs, fill, seal into half-moons (crimp edges).
Deep fry on medium until golden.
Cool and store in airtight box — Holi essential.

tips: Low flame frying cooks the centre without burning.
recipes.name: Thekua
steps: Melt jaggery with little water; cool slightly.
Mix flour, fennel, coconut, ghee and jaggery syrup into a stiff dough.
Shape into patterned discs (use mould or fork).
Deep fry on medium-low until deep brown and cooked inside.
Chhath and festive prasadam across Purvanchal.

tips: Coarse texture is traditional — not a fine powder.
recipes.name: Churma

ingredients.name: Wheat flour baatis or coarse crushed roti

steps: Crush baked baatis or thick ghee rotis coarsely.
Mix with warm ghee, powdered sugar/jaggery and cardamom.
Adjust sweetness.
Garnish with nuts.
Serve with dal baati or as dessert.

tips: Adjust sweetness/spice to family taste.
recipes.name: Lauki Halwa
steps: Grate lauki and squeeze lightly. Cook in ghee 5 minutes.
Add milk; cook until lauki soft and milk reduces.
Add sugar and cardamom; cook until thick.
Add khoya optional.
Garnish with nuts.

tips: Adjust sweetness/spice to family taste.
recipes.name: Besan Ladoo
steps: Roast besan in ghee until aromatic and golden.
Cool slightly; mix powdered sugar and cardamom.
Shape into ladoos while still warm.
Set aside to firm.
Festive classic.

tips: Adjust sweetness/spice to family taste.
recipes.name: Coconut Ladoo
steps: Cook grated coconut with condensed milk or sugar syrup.
Add cardamom; cook until sticky.
Shape ladoos; roll in coconut.
Cool to set.
Quick sweet.

tips: Adjust sweetness/spice to family taste.
recipes.name: Vegetable Soup
steps: Boil mixed vegetables with ginger and pepper.
Blend half for body; keep half chunky.
Season with salt and lemon.
Serve hot as light dinner starter.
Comforting when someone is unwell.

tips: Adjust sweetness/spice to family taste.
recipes.name: Corn Chaat
steps: Boil sweet corn; drain.
Mix onion, tomato, chilli, chaat masala, lemon and salt.
Serve immediately.
Optional butter.
Quick evening snack.

tips: Adjust sweetness/spice to family taste.
recipes.name: Sprouts Chaat
steps: Steam moong/chana sprouts lightly.
Mix with onion, tomato, chutneys and spices.
Finish with sev.
Healthy chaat.
Do not oversteam sprouts.

tips: Adjust sweetness/spice to family taste.
recipes.name: Tomato Rasam
steps: Cook tomatoes with tamarind, rasam spices and dal water.
Temper mustard and curry leaves.
Serve with rice or as soup.
Digestive and light.
South Indian comfort.

tips: Adjust sweetness/spice to family taste.
recipes.name: Cabbage Sabzi
steps: Temper cumin; add shredded cabbage and spices.
Cook open to evaporate moisture.
Finish with garam masala.
Simple everyday sabzi.
Do not cover too long.

tips: Adjust sweetness/spice to family taste.
recipes.name: Beans Poriyal
steps: Cook chopped beans with turmeric and salt until tender-crisp.
Temper mustard and curry leaves.
Add grated coconut.
South Indian dry vegetable.
Keep beans bright green.

tips: Adjust sweetness/spice to family taste.
recipes.name: Onion Tomato Sabzi
steps: Sauté lots of onion until soft.
Add tomato and spices; cook until jammy.
Everyday emergency sabzi when fridge is empty.
Serve with roti.
Add potato if available.
